description: A database of groundwater wells in the United States is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Chung-Yi Lin et al. Groundwater wells are critical infrastructure that enable the monitoring, extraction, and use of groundwater, which has important implications for the environment, water security, and economic development. Despite the importance of wells, a unified database collecting and standardizing information on the characteristics and locations of these wells across the United States has been lacking. Coverage: national (US); published in 2024. Formats: CSV, Python, ZIP, Excel, Shapefile. The data are held in Consortium of Universities for the Advancement of Hydrologic Science, Inc and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 3871970657 bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is This resource is shared under the Creative Commons Attribution CC BY., taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support water-network, drainage and hydraulic studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
